description: PROP-P7a (grep -l "PushNotification" across the 8 target files) and PROP-P7b (adversary reads the added sentence's wording) only prove the literal string is present somewhere in the file and that its wording is semantically correct. Neither tier proves the added line is actually inside the runtime prompt/task variable that reaches `claude -p` / `claude --model sonnet -- "$STARTUP"` for the spawned session. A comment, a dead branch, or a line placed outside the quoted prompt string would satisfy both PROP-P7a and PROP-P7b while never being seen by the spawned model. This is not hypothetical for one of the 8 files: on-disk verification shows `~/anicca/skills/_shared/adversary-daily.sh` builds its prompt via `PROMPT=$(sed ... "$PROMPT_TMPL" 2>/dev/null || echo "Review feature ${SLOT} per ...")`, where `$PROMPT_TMPL` points to `~/anicca/skills/_shared/adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl` -- a file that does NOT exist on disk (`ls` confirms). So the script currently always falls through to the short hardcoded `echo` fallback as the actual `$PROMPT`. Any implementer who adds the PushNotification instruction as, say, a script comment near line 23 (next to the `--model opus` edit from REQ-P5a) or inside the unused sed/tmpl branch would pass `grep -l "PushNotification" adversary-daily.sh` and would pass an adversary wording-check of that added text, yet the spawned `claude -p` session would never receive the instruction because it isn't part of the executed `$PROMPT` value. The other 7 files (self-fix.sh TASK=..., clip-cli.sh/capafy-loop-cli.sh/reddit-loop-cli.sh/clip-promote-cli.sh/video-cli.sh STARTUP=...) are simpler single quoted-string assignments where this risk is lower but still not mechanically excluded by the current PROP-P7a/PROP-P7b wording.
suggestedFix: Add an explicit verification criterion (shell where possible, judgment otherwise) that the added PushNotification line is textually inside the specific variable/string literal that is passed as the prompt argument to the `claude` invocation in each of the 8 files (e.g. grep for the string between the opening quote of `TASK="`/`STARTUP='` and its matching closing quote, or instruct the adversary explicitly to trace each file's `claude -p`/`claude --model sonnet --` invocation back to confirm the added sentence is part of the exact argument passed at runtime, not merely present in the file). For `_shared/adversary-daily.sh` specifically, call out in the requirement that the missing `adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl` means the actual runtime prompt is currently the `echo` fallback string, and require the added line to be placed inside that fallback string (or otherwise guarantee it's unconditionally appended to `$PROMPT` after the `sed`/fallback resolves, regardless of which branch fires).
